scenario: LEXP.7.20: a schema-typed slot names one fact, and keeps naming it after that fact leaves working memory; a fact re-asserted with the same key is another fact ([LFAC.2.5.3]), so the slot does not name it. The Child is a `ttl` fact emitted unconditionally, so retracting its parent does not retract it. Pump 1: Seed, Parent 1, Parent 2; `make` emits the Child naming Parent 1; `eq` fires with Parent 1 and `ne` with Parent 2. Then the Seed and Parent 1 are retracted and Parent 1 is asserted again, as a new fact. Pump 2: `ne` fires for the new Parent 1, and `eq` does not. Exactly ["eq 1/1", "ne 1/2", "ne 1/1"]. A runtime that compared keys would log `eq 1/1` in pump 2. One that read a slot naming a fact no longer in working memory as `null` would log nothing in pump 2, by null propagation. PATH PINNED: the slot read returns the stored reference unchanged (libds `rete/eval.c` DS_RETE_EXPR_VAR returns `f->slots[si]`, a FACT_REF holding the target's rete id, and ids are never reused; Mercury `ds.eval` `slot_value` returns the stored `fact_ref`), and the comparison is by id (libds `val_eq_unordered`, Mercury `compare_outcome`).
rules_ds:
schema Seed scope logical:
    n: Int key

schema Parent scope logical:
    id: Int key

schema Child scope ttl 1_h:
    id: Int
    parent: Parent

rule make:
    Seed
    Parent p where p.id == 1
->
    emit Child id: 1 parent: p

rule eq:
    Child c
    Parent p where c.parent == p
->
    log info "eq {c.id}/{p.id}"

rule ne:
    Child c
    Parent p where c.parent != p
->
    log info "ne {c.id}/{p.id}"
